title: Split String Into Non-Overlapping Label Blocks
statement:
You are given a string that consists only of lowercase English letters. Your task is to cut the string into the smallest possible number of contiguous, non-overlapping pieces (reading left to right, together covering every character exactly once) so that each distinct letter appears in only one of the pieces.

In other words, if a letter shows up multiple times in the string, every occurrence of that letter must fall inside the same piece, no letter is allowed to be split across two pieces.

Among all ways of cutting the string that satisfy this rule, return the sequence of piece lengths, listed in the order the pieces occur, when the string is cut into as many pieces as possible while still respecting the rule.

examples.explanation: The letter 'a' first appears at index 0 and last appears at index 2, 'b' only at index 1, 'c' spans indices 2 to 6 (with 'z' also nested inside that range), so the first cut must include indices 0-4 -> "abacc" (length 5). Next, 'z' occupies index 5 and 'c' already closed, giving "z" alone... but since 'c' also appears at index 6 which stretches the boundary, the first valid block becomes indices 0-4 ("abacc"). The remaining string "zcdde" splits into "zc" wait, recomputing carefully: the greedy scan yields blocks "abacc" (5), "zc" is invalid since c already used... The actual correct greedy result for this string is [5,3,2], corresponding to "abacc", "zcd", "de".

'x' appears at indices 0 and 1 only, so the first block "xx" (length 2) can close immediately after index 1. Then 'y' appears only at index 2, forming its own block "y" (length 1). Finally 'z' appears only at index 3, forming the last block "z" (length 1).

constraints: s consists of lowercase English letters only
